title: The metta sutta in Pali
hookLine: a parent who loses a child in a store for ten seconds: could that care point at strangers?
tomorrow: what counts as the highest blessing? not what you'd guess.

cards: A parent loses sight of a small child in a grocery store for ten seconds, and turns into a searchlight. The cart doesn't matter. The line doesn't matter.
Who's watching doesn't matter. There's only the scanning, aisle after aisle, until a small head appears by the cereal.
A short Buddhist discourse takes that exact searchlight and asks one question: how wide could it reach? Could it point at strangers?

teach.h: KARANIYAM: THIS IS TO BE DONE.
teach.b: The Metta Sutta opens like a to-do list: karaniyam atthakusalena. This is to be done by one skilled in good.
Then it says what that person is like: capable, upright, straight, gentle in speech, not proud, content, easy to look after. Character first.
Then the wish spreads out in rings: may all beings be happy, weak or strong, large or small, seen or unseen, near or far, born or yet to be born. And then the image.

teach.h: A MOTHER AND HER ONLY CHILD.
teach.b: Just as a mother would guard her only child with her own life, so, the sutta says, grow a boundless heart toward all beings. The searchlight, aimed at strangers. Now a neighbor tradition.

teach.h: GURU ARJAN: NO ONE IS A STRANGER.
teach.b: In the Guru Granth Sahib, the Sikh scripture, Guru Arjan sings that since finding the company of the holy, his envy of others is gone: no one is my enemy, and no one is a stranger; I get along with everyone.
Two traditions, one shared hope: care so wide nobody is left outside it. And one honest difference.

teach.h: ONE GOD IN ALL, OR A HEART TRAINED.
teach.b: In Guru Arjan's hymn, that wide heart comes through holy company, and he sees the one God pervading everyone. The Metta Sutta names no creator; its wide heart is something you train, like any skill.

how: Theravada Buddhists chant the Karaniya Metta Sutta in Pali at temples, at blessings and at home, and its lines are used in metta meditation, wishing well to themselves, loved ones, strangers and all beings.

games.q: what does “the metta sutta in pali” mean?
o: the Buddha's discourse on growing goodwill toward all
a blessing chanted over a newborn by its mother
the Buddha's advice on choosing good friends

games.q: the Metta Sutta — tap the pairs.
p: guarding her only child with her life
no one is my enemy, no one a stranger

s: the Metta Sutta is only about sitting and sending good wishes
it opens with conduct: capable, upright, gentle in speech, content. character first, then the wish.
the sutta's wish reaches beings born and yet to be born
weak or strong, seen or unseen, near or far, born or yet to be born.
the Sikh line and the Metta Sutta say exactly the same thing
they share a hope: no one left outside care. Guru Arjan sees the one God in all; the sutta trains a heart and names no creator.

games.q: a new kid has eaten lunch alone every day this week. you don't know him. by the Metta Sutta, what's the move?
o: wish him well silently; metta happens inside your head.
treat him with the care you'd want for your own, starting with a hello.
wait until he's part of your group; care starts with your people.
games.why: the sutta opens with conduct and ends with a mother's care aimed at all beings, strangers included. the wish and the hello belong together.

practice: Chant the first line once: karaniyam atthakusalena. Then look at the nearest door, and hold whoever walks through it next in mind, a family member, a coworker, a stranger.
For the sit, wish them what the sutta wishes: may you be happy, may you be safe.

wordCard.voice: The metta sutta in Pali: karaniyam atthakusalena, this is to be done by one skilled in good. Character first, then a heart with no edges.

orig.note: Pali, in Devanagari letters: karaniyam, to be done; attha, good; kusalena, by one skilled.

carryVoice: The line to keep: skilled in good, a skill you can practice on the next stranger. Day 1448, done.

sources.ref: Sutta Nipata 1.8 (Karaniya Metta Sutta): karaniyam atthakusalena; the qualities; may all beings be happy; as a mother would guard her only child with her life, so a boundless heart toward all beings

Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1299 (Guru Arjan, Raag Kaanraa): since finding the company of the holy, envy of others is forgotten; no one is my enemy, no one a stranger; I get along with all; the one God pervades all
